operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table names: 'Companies', 'Office_locations' vs lowercase 'buildings'; column 'City' capitalized, others lowercase — identifier quoting must preserve original case.
All columns declared NOT NULL=0 (nullable) yet original null_rate=0.0 everywhere; TS will happily emit NULLs, so inserts succeed but semantics shift.
Market_Value_billion declared TEXT but stores numeric strings ('182.2'); TS String fuzzer will produce non-numeric text, breaking numeric comparisons.
move_in_year declared INT (dispatches to Number, not Year/Date) though values are years 2021-2025; TS Number range [-10^0,10^0] default scale gives tiny ints, not years.
Office_locations has composite PK (building_id, company_id) — TS composite-PK member max_l0=30 cap applies; PK dedup must drop duplicate pairs.
Two FKs from Office_locations to buildings.id and Companies.id; both parents exist and are unique PKs — clean FK graph, no dangling/self refs.
Tiny tables (12/19/16 rows): original_values sampling k=min(5,len) gives 5 of 12-19; literal pool from train SQL is the main value source.
buildings.id and Companies.id are INT PKs with distinct=rows (no gaps visible in samples 1..5); TS Number PK generation will produce non-contiguous, possibly negative ids.
No indexes/views/triggers beyond PKs; DDL clone is trivial.
REAL columns (Sales/Profits/Assets_billion) have wide magnitudes (up to 2467.9); TS Number scale=0 default range [-1,1] is far off — implausible values likely.
Status/City/Industry/Headquarters are low-cardinality enums (2-8 distinct) stored as free text; TS String fuzzer ignores the enum.
No text-stored dates anywhere; no crash-fallback declared types (all map to Number/String).
operator_ts_expectations: id columns: Number fuzzer, int scale=0, range [-1,1] plus ±1/±2 perturbation — produces tiny/negative ids, not 1..19; PK dedup keeps first occurrence so few rows survive.
name/Headquarters/Industry/Status/City: String fuzzer, random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0-20 with 50% contamination — implausible business names, drives FN on name filters.
Sales/Profits/Assets_billion: Number float scale=0, range [-1,1] — values ~100-2500 in original become ~[-1,1]; any threshold query (Sales>100) returns empty → FN.
Market_Value_billion: String fuzzer on TEXT column — emits random letters, so numeric comparisons/aggregations on it error or mismatch → FP/FN.
move_in_year: Number int, range [-1,1] — year filters (move_in_year=2021) never match → FN; range queries (BETWEEN 2020 AND 2025) empty.
Office_locations FK columns draw from parent final id lists (tiny/negative) with replacement; composite PK dedup then drops many rows → small join cardinality, missing ties → FP on COUNT/DISTINCT.
buildings.Height/Stories: Number int range [-1,1] — height/story thresholds (Height>200) empty → FN.
Low-cardinality enums (City 2, Status 3, Industry 5) replaced by random strings → GROUP BY produces ~n groups instead of 2-3, DISTINCT counts wrong → FP.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python; nullable columns may get NULLs from empty parent FK lists, changing join semantics.
Original has no duplicate PKs and unique FKs; TS may create ties in non-PK columns (e.g. same City string) that original lacks → FP on equality joins.
Small tables mean TS sizes (30-2500) vastly exceed original 12-19 rows — cardinality-sensitive queries (COUNT=12) fail → FN.
Literal pool from train SQL anchors values to FK roots; with no FK chains beyond Office_locations, pool values mostly land on id columns, not on text enums.
